hypotheses.H1_backdating_boundary: An insertion backdated by d <= 30 s into a sealed second is never attributable (the verifier reports it as a late commit, or has no evidence when the second was not sealed yet); d = 45 s is always attributable; at d = 33 s exactly when the monitor copied the recorder within the 3 s before the insertion committed.
hypotheses.H2_insertion_only_reattribution: An automation_triggered event sharing a sealed actuation's context, inserted with a timestamp just before it at 5, 15 or 25 s after the actuation, moves the actuation's displayed cause (frontend display rule) to the automation and is not attributable; at 45 s it is attributable (R3 Q2).
hypotheses.H3_observation_window: A deletion is detected if and only if an observable poll read the row before it was deleted; the detection rate rises with the delay as about delay / poll interval and is 1 for delays above the longest poll interval.
hypotheses.H4_phase_aware_deletion: An in-hub adversary senses the direct-read monitor's reads (another process's lock on the recorder's -shm) and, deleting 0.3 s before the predicted next read, escapes M-direct at visible times at which the non-adaptive deletion is mostly detected.
hypotheses.H5_reused_lower_key: A row inserted with a reused lower key into a sealed second is always detected (R1 Q1).
hypotheses.H6_purge_window: Under a declared purge (tolerance 60 s): purge-shaped deletion of the tolerance band is excused (by design); deletion of a recent row, of rows just beyond the band, an out-of-order band deletion, and a forged old row first observed after scheduled + 120 s are detected; a forged old row inserted and deleted inside the 120 s window is not detected (excused as a purged row, or no evidence if no poll saw it).
hypotheses.H7_sustained_unobservability: A write lock held by a second connection blinds neither monitor (WAL readers) but delays the hub's commits, and rows committed more than 30 s late are attributable; a POSIX write lock on the -shm DMS byte makes every direct read unobservable for the hold without stopping the hub, while copy mode observes; an unread table of about 3 GiB added to the recorder blinds copy mode (copy_raced) until a repack and not direct mode; window inflation slows polls without unobservability. An edit of a row sealed before a blind window is detected; a row written and deleted inside it is not detected by the blinded monitor. The pre-registered rule flags every attack-caused unobservable interval and no interval of E9's benign week.
hypotheses.H8_D1_live: A row backdated across a blind window of M-direct into a second sealed before it is a late commit for the E9 verifier (escape), unknown for the patched verifier, and attributable on M-copy.
hypotheses.H9_D2_D1h_offline_collusion: With the record(s) carrying an emptied second's root and keylog ranges withheld, the E9 verifier reads the second as match and the patched verifier as unknown; with the polls between a 45 s-backdated row's sealing and its insertion withheld, the E9 verifier reads match and the patched verifier unknown.
hypotheses.H10_D3_clock_step: Rows the hub writes during a 60 s backward clock step are attributable without a marker and excused under an operator CLOCK_STEP marker; a 10 s step raises no violation.
hypotheses.H11_entity_id_rename: Renaming an entity id fails every sealed second, minute and hour holding a row of that entity, in the numbers predicted from the recorder, and no marker excuses it; the RENAME marker excuses its name-map transition.
hypotheses.H12_device_removal: Removing a device changes no recorder row (no violation); its name-map transition is excused by the declared RENAME marker.
hypotheses.H13_entity_history_purge: Purging an entity's history fails every sealed segment holding its rows (predicted from the recorder); no marker excuses it.
hypotheses.H14_upgrades: 2025.11.1 -> 2026.7.4 (schema 51 -> 53) and 2026.7.4 -> 2026.10.1 (53) change no committed row: no violation over the whole sealed history; schema_changes gains 52 and 53 in the first.
hypotheses.H15_hardening: On honest recorders the hardened monitor's records equal E9's (tests) and no E10 poll fails with schema_object_not_a_table or quick_check_failed; re-verifying E7, E8 and E9 with the patched verifier changes no flagged second and every other difference has a listed reason.
hypotheses.H16_benign_floor: No flagged second of the main session is unexplained by an arm.
hypotheses.H17_sham_specificity: With the attack integration's write rolled back on the code paths of A1-BDT (45 s), A2-CTX (45 s) and A3-DEL (10 s), at the same timing and in the same session, no violation is attributable to any of the 90 sham trials on either monitor: its would-be target second is not flagged, its own actuation row is not attributable and no keylog violation names it (0 of 90 per monitor); at the same levels the attack trials' target seconds are violated.
hypotheses.H18_restart_mid_poll: A hub restart, graceful or killed, whose effect lands inside a monitor's read (direct) or copy (copy) window, raises no attributable row and no flagged second on either monitor and restarts no monitor; rows committed around it are benign_late under the E9 verifier and benign_late or unobserved_late under the patched verifier (unobserved_late exactly when an unobservable or missing poll or a gap above GAP_S lies in the row's bracket, D1); no unobservable interval it causes is flagged by the distinguishability rule; the recorder is never moved away.
hypotheses.H19_dz_switchtype: A benign switch-type change of the Domoticz lock (19 -> 20) by its owner through the hub's own API makes every anchored second, minute and hour segment that holds a log row of the lock and was first anchored before the change a violation, and no other segment; the offline root comparison changes exactly those seconds; the platform's renderer shows the lock's earlier rows differently; no marker excuses it (a measured limit of a closure that commits a configuration field).
hypotheses.H20_pairwise_closure: No pair of mutations (exhaustive same-target pairs at E8B's primary values; samples of 1,000 other-value pairs and 1,000 cross-row pairs) changes the rendered output while leaving the deployed stable-columns commitment unchanged; no pair of fields that each leave the output unchanged changes it jointly; no field outside E8B's 27-field closure changes the output once another field changed. Line and branch coverage of the logbook package is reported, with the branch sites never taken.
hypotheses.H21_pi4_cost: Under the Pi 4-class profile the direct-read monitor's median poll stays below PERIOD (5 s) at 0.19 GB and 0.96 GB with no poll above GAP_S (30 s) except a due quick_check; copy mode writes about the recorder's size per poll (bytes written per hour reported); the pi4 / ref ratio of the median poll time is reported per size. Exploratory where it depends on the assumed limits (no prediction at 2.94 GB).

analysis_plan: No hypothesis test beyond the exact intervals; every prediction is stated per trial or per count above and is confirmed only if every non-excluded trial agrees (an unpredicted outcome is reported with its trial, not averaged away)
Both monitors are scored separately; nothing is pooled across them
Every deviation from this registration (plan, parameters, code) is written to an amendment before it is used, as for E9
known_limits_stated_in_advance: Scratch stacks on one Mac with virtual devices; the lab installation is not touched
The clock step is emulated inside the hub's process (time.time), not a host clock step
No release after 2026.7.4 changes the recorder schema; the schema arm crosses 51 -> 53 on a fresh install, whose SQLite steps touch statistics_meta only
The phase sensor is specific to direct read on one kernel (the hub and the monitor share Docker's VM)
Lock-based blinding depends on SQLite's unix VFS behaviour (3.40.1 in the monitor image); exploratory arms carry no prediction
review r5: the sham runs as one block, not interleaved with the attack trials; it shares their session, monitors and hub but not their minutes
